messages:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT [SEV2] Private VPC ILB cross-region failures — elevated 5xx for customers with cross-region routing (eu-west1 -> us-central1). Triggered by ILB healthcheck flaps and backend ejection. Pager: Maria H.
Maria H.: seeing spike in 5xx at ~10:12 UTC, healthchecks failing on control-plane proxies. Affected tenants: 3 large, 2 mid. Support already paging.
Kevin L.: adding context — metric spike in egress to metadata /token endpoints from auth filter, also large backlog at our observability ingestion (significant latency).
Samir P.: suspect GCP metadata server throttling + our auth provider token refresh causing storms. Correlating with >50k requests/min to metadata endpoints from private-vpc proxies.
NetEng: am starting connectivity checks between ILB and proxies, and validating route propagation (no recent routing changes).
ObservabilityBot: PERF_ALERT: metric-ingest-latency > 120s for "ingest-proxy"; trace sampling dropped to 1% — might obscure debugging.
Maria H.: immediate mitigation options: 1) disable auth-filter token refresh on cross-region path 2) divert traffic to regional-only route for impacted customers 3) increase ILB backend draining timeout. Which can we do fastest?
Kevin L.: (oncall) I'll try diverting routes to regional ILB first — less risk. Samir, can you prepare a config to pin to eu-west1?
Samir P.: preparing route override. Will update gcp routing policy and push canary. Estimated 6-8m.
Seán O.: FYI GCP support is open on my side, I can file a network incident referencing METADATA QUOTA. Who will create the support case?
Maria H.: Seán please do it, include project ids and sample request traces. Also escalate to GCP SE — this looks like metadata server rate-limiting hits from our proxies.
Support Lead: drafting a customer-facing blurb now: short impact summary, mitigations, ETA. Send to me for review.
NetEng: running quick healthcheck curl against ILB health endpoint: 
```
curl -v --resolve internal-ilb.privatevpc:80:10.10.0.5 http://internal-ilb.privatevpc/health
```
response intermittently 502/504. backend TCP OK but application 502.
Kevin L.: routed 20% of traffic for two affected tenants to eu-west1-only via routing policy change (canary). Monitoring.
ObservabilityBot: Route-change detected: traffic_shift eu-west1 +20% -> OK. 5xx rate down 35% for those tenants.
Samir P.: pushing full regional pin for impacted customers now. Rolling change: 
```
# gcloud example
gcloud compute forwarding-rules update internal-ilb-fr --region=eu-west1 --targets=<regional-target-pool>
```
Expected cooldown ~5m.
Maria H.: parallel mitigation: temporarily disable token-refresh middleware in auth-proxy for private-vpc cross-region routes. Kevin, are we comfortable disabling?
Kevin L.: yes for cross-region only — do it. Samir, coordinate to avoid overlapping config pushes.
Samir P.: disabling token refresh, leaving cached tokens for 10m TTL. Patch applied.
ObservabilityBot: metric-ingest-latency improving; token-refresh calls to metadata endpoint down 78%.
GCP Oncall: Support case created (case# 123456789). GCP notes suspected metadata server rate-limit at project level; they see spikes from our proxies — recommending throttle on client side.
Maria H.: customers still see intermittent errors but severity reduced. Support lead, please update customers with current status: we've applied regional routing and token-refresh reduction; working with GCP to remediate quota.
Support Lead: posting to affected customers now: short note + link to incident status page.
Kevin L.: handoff to night oncall (Seán) in 30m. I'll prepare a concise handover with current mitigations and next actions.
Seán O.: taking handoff. Will keep watch for 2 hours and coordinate with GCP Oncall.
Maria H.: action items for post-incident: - follow up with GCP on permanent quota increase or design change - add client-side exponential backoff in auth-proxy - add observability alert for metadata endpoint QPS per project - create runbook for cross-region token storms. Assign owners.
Samir P.: noted, I'll own backoff implementation (ticket #INC-8932).
Kevin L.: I'll own runbook update and customer comms postmortem.
ObservabilityBot: NOTE: saved snapshot of traces and metrics to incident artifact bundle: s3://redwood-incidents/2076543210/snapshot.zip
pagerduty-bot: Incident severity downgraded to SEV3 at 10:47 UTC — traffic stable for pinned routes, ongoing backend monitoring.
Maria H.: closing steps: keep oncall Seán watching; plan for dedicated rate-limits in our private-vpc proxies to avoid hitting metadata quotas in future.
Seán O.: will keep watch and escalate if regression. Leaving this thread open for RCA notes.
Support Lead: final customer update queued for 11:15 UTC after we confirm GCP next steps.
Maria H.: great work team — postmortem owner Kevin L., tech owner Samir P., timeline & comms owner Maria H. Everyone please add notes to the incident doc.
Kevin L.: quick question for follow-up: do we want temporary increase to token cache TTL globally or route-specific? Propose route-specific first.
Samir P.: agree route-specific. Will prototype and submit PR.
Maria H.: thanks. Ending live paging — incident remains monitored and will transition to follow-up channel. :white_check_mark:
